headline: Why Britain prefers foreign-owned public utilities
standfirst: The UK is open to public ownership, but typically only when it is backed by foreign

steps.label: What happened
steps.text: The UK often allows foreign entities to own public infrastructure like energy grids.

steps.label: How we got here
steps.text: This pattern stems from historical reliance on private systems, notably for gas boilers.

steps.label: Why it matters
steps.text: Experts argue a rapid energy transition requires a new, mutualised approach to ownership.

steps.label: What to watch
steps.text: Future debates on whether domestic public control can replace foreign-led models.

caption:
Why is Britain more comfortable with foreign ownership of public utilities than domestic public ownership?

Author Arthur Downing notes that our current energy infrastructure relies heavily on legacy systems like gas boilers. Moving toward a green future may require rethinking who actually owns the grid. It is a complex issue of policy and national infrastructure strategy.
